VEO-IBD (very-early onset IBD) is a particularly severe form of inflammatory bowel disease that affects the youngest children [^src1]. Due to the patients' age and the severity of the condition, VEO-IBD often requires highly specialized diagnostic approaches [^src1]. In Denmark, the diagnostic care for these young patients is centralized and managed by the three largest university departments, which include [[hvidovre|Hvidovre]], Odense, and Aarhus [^src1].

Within the broader national effort to standardize and improve IBD diagnostics through the DANIBD database, VEO-IBD is a critical factor in evaluating quality Indicator 1b, which applies to children and adolescents [^src1]. The condition specifically helps explain deviations from standard diagnostic pathways, such as the omission of small intestine MRI scans. Because performing an MRI on very young children typically requires anesthesia, the medical need to limit anesthesia exposure often results in the scan being skipped, which directly impacts the fulfillment rates of Indicator 1b [^src1]. Understanding these clinical realities is essential for accurately interpreting regional variations and shaping future national and international guidelines for pediatric IBD care [^src1].
